props.statement: The glow of chromium-gel precipitates differs fundamentally from the glow of ZnO-CrO3 catalysts during reduction: it is not affected by the atmosphere (oxidizing, reducing, inert or vacuum); its onset (420-620 °C) depends on the preparation conditions and its temperature rise on the heating rate; ageing has no effect.

props.name: weight loss unrelated to the glow

evidence.note: 'Fig. 1 shows a thermal decomposition curve of the precipitate made by adding aqueous ammonia to chromium nitrate solution. This sample glows at 590 °C, but no weight change is seen near 590 °C; only losses, mainly dehydration, below 300 °C and near 380-390 °C.'; quote withheld: sha256:0212644d8f0c0296c9f9a03aee53834165f0645cf1da3fd3903a6708a717d467 chars:129

'Molstad et al. reported a weight decrease of about 40% at the glow; this weight decrease can be said to be unrelated to the glow.' (Molstad's figure is cited, not this source's measurement.); quote withheld: sha256:5e0934ddcc8a585fe29d675db16bf6301085b70ff22a4f09b06652ec43339485 chars:72

props.note: Molstad's 40% is cited, not measured here.
props.statement: The ammonia-precipitated chromium gel glows at 590 °C with no weight change near 590 °C (losses, mainly dehydration, only below 300 °C and near 380-390 °C); so a weight decrease at the glow, such as the about 40% reported by Molstad et al., is unrelated to the glow.

props.name: reduced catalyst structurally differs from lower oxides

evidence.note: '(In the previous report) ZnO-CrO3 catalysts after reduction are bright blue-green, quite unlike the colour of the lower oxides made by high-temperature treatment in air or vacuum, so a structural difference was surmised.' '高柵' = 高温.; quote withheld: sha256:9f70e6123bc6af795db5230d2c9eb7d52d1603a318e829d50a374374a97e8a77 chars:99

props.note: The colour observation is from the previous report (ref. 1); the source does not state an explicit verdict on this surmise.
props.statement: Because the reduced ZnO-CrO3 catalyst is bright blue-green, unlike the lower oxides made by high-temperature treatment in air or vacuum, the two differ in structure.

props.name: heat of the transition of the reduced structure may cause the glow

evidence.note: 'If the reduced catalyst has a special structure and transforms at high temperature into a more stable one, it would naturally be accompanied by heat evolution that could cause the glow.' '発勲' = 発熱.; quote withheld: sha256:df312e709a4390794f3e43a07dbecba3a54be9f12c85c33ee80334f2989d8128 chars:72

Abstract: 'Hence, since a transition to stable zinc oxide and spinel is observed, both catalysts are thought to evolve heat more or less.'; quote withheld: sha256:11ef7a8903ad975fa6f67d3cc02ff714d6b4257f684b2dedd2ad474e30817157 chars:66

Abstract: 'Depending on the size of this heat one could decide whether the structural change is the main cause of the glow or a secondary accompanying cause; this will be reported later.'; quote withheld: sha256:7f59878b00902ff5551fa4e6fa8d44a347bbceeb8aa5679d0fb22fdefff919d8 chars:86

props.statement: If the reduced catalyst has a special structure that transforms at high temperature into a more stable one (zinc oxide and spinel), heat is evolved that could cause the glow; both ZnO-CrO3 and Zn(NO3)2-Cr(NO3)3 catalysts should evolve heat more or less, and whether the structural change is the main or a secondary cause of the glow is left to a later report.
